page: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is a general-purpose instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 1 physical core and 1 vCPU running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with no hyperthreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, resulting in a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the top 25% at 3031.88. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core score in the bottom 10% to 25%. Memory bandwidth write large block and single-threaded gzip compression perform at average levels, while read-only memory bandwidth and Passmark memory scores are in the lower percentiles.

Given its single dedicated core and DDR5 memory, the m7a.medium offers an entry-level entry point into the AMD EPYC Gen7 family, providing dedicated CPU resources without the burstable performance degradation of shared-core instances. It is suitable for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high multi-core throughput or local storage.
